epox_morsch.cite: Soderberg, Organic Chemistry with a Biological Emphasis, via LibreTexts 9.15 Reactions of Epoxides (Morsch, UIS CHE 267)
epox_morsch.says: Basic/alkoxide opening is SN2 at the least hindered epoxide carbon; acid-catalysed opening has SN1 character and attack is at the more substituted carbon; both with backside attack.

epox_wade.cite: Wade, Organic Chemistry, via LibreTexts 15.08 Opening of Epoxides
epox_wade.says: Anhydrous HX gives trans halohydrins; halide attacks the less substituted carbon if both are primary/secondary but the tertiary carbon if one carbon is tertiary; aqueous acid gives glycols by anti opening.

epox_chan.cite: LibreTexts 11.4 Opening of Epoxides (Chan, UIUC Chem 2363A)
epox_chan.says: Same text as Wade: HX opens epoxides to trans halohydrins with attack at tertiary carbon when present.

epox_ssu.cite: LibreTexts 18.6 Reactions of Epoxides: Ring-opening (SSU Chem 335A)
epox_ssu.says: Aqueous-acid cleavage of epoxides gives trans glycols; HX gives trans halohydrins with tertiary-carbon attack.

epox_grig.cite: Wade, LibreTexts 15.09 Reactions of Epoxides with Grignard and Organolithium Reagents
epox_grig.says: Grignard opening of epoxides follows the same SN2 mechanism as base-promoted opening (strong nucleophile and base), with inversion.

e2_cyclohexane.cite: OpenStax Organic Chemistry 11.9 via LibreTexts: The E2 Reaction and Cyclohexane Conformation
e2_cyclohexane.says: Neomenthyl chloride gives 3-menthene and eliminates 200x faster than menthyl chloride, which must ring-flip and gives 2-menthene (non-Zaitsev) via its only trans-diaxial hydrogen.

mom_e2.cite: Master Organic Chemistry, The E2 Reaction and Cyclohexane Rings
mom_e2.says: Neomenthyl chloride gives 78% 3-menthene and 22% 2-menthene with EtO- in ethanol (Hughes/Ingold/Rose, JACS 1955); E2 needs axial leaving group and axial anti H.

wiki_zaitsev.says: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane with NaOEt gives the Zaitsev product; bulky bases such as KOtBu favour the Hofmann product.

hofmann_wiki.says: Heating a quaternary ammonium hydroxide gives the less substituted (Hofmann) alkene as major product.

eas_uis.cite: LibreTexts 18.07 EAS of Substituted Benzenes (Morsch and Andrews, UIS CHE 269)
eas_uis.says: Nitration of tert-butylbenzene gives 16% ortho, 8% meta, 75% para (steric hindrance at ortho); toluene gives 58.5% o, 37% p, 4.5% m.

eas_poly.cite: McMurry, LibreTexts 16.6 Trisubstituted Benzenes - Additivity of Effects
eas_poly.says: Reinforcing (cooperative) directing groups give the summed result; when directing effects oppose, the substituent with a lone pair on the ring atom normally controls the site.

fc_limits.cite: LibreTexts 18.10 Limitations on Electrophilic Substitution Reactions with Substituted Benzenes (SSU Chem 335B)
fc_limits.says: Friedel-Crafts fails on strongly deactivated rings such as nitrobenzene; acetanilide nitrates at low temperature to give the para-nitro product in high yield.

wiki_nitr.says: Direct nitration of aniline with HNO3/H2SO4 gives, per one source, a roughly 50/50 mixture of para and meta isomers (anilinium formation, plus oxidation).

cation_morsch.cite: Morsch et al., LibreTexts 7.12 Evidence for the Mechanism of Electrophilic Additions: Carbocation Rearrangements
cation_morsch.says: HBr adds to 3-methyl-1-butene to give mainly 2-bromo-2-methylbutane via hydride shift, not the Markovnikov 2-bromo-3-methylbutane.

cation_alc.says: Because alcohol ionisation proceeds through carbocations, hydride or alkyl shifts relocate the cation to a more stable position.

wiki_wm.says: Acid-promoted dehydration of isoborneol gives camphene via Wagner-Meerwein shift.

wiki_pinacol.says: Under acid, pinacol (a 1,2-diol) rearranges to pinacolone.

wiki_hbo.says: Hydroboration-oxidation is syn addition of H and OH, anti-Markovnikov, OH on the less substituted carbon.

br2_liu.cite: Liu, LibreTexts 10.4 Addition of Bromine and Chlorine to Alkenes
br2_liu.says: Br2 adds anti: (E)-2-butene gives meso (2R,3S)-2,3-dibromobutane; (Z)-2-butene gives the racemic (2S,3S)/(2R,3R) pair.

prilezhaev.says: Peracid epoxidation transfers alkene geometry with fidelity: trans-2-butene gives trans-2,3-epoxybutane.

sn2_roberts.cite: Roberts and Caserio, LibreTexts 8.6 Stereochemistry of SN2 Reactions
sn2_roberts.says: SN2 proceeds by back-side attack with inversion of configuration (hydroxide on 2-chlorobutane gives inverted 2-butanol).

sn2_wade.cite: Wade, LibreTexts 7.7 Stereochemistry of the SN2 Reaction
sn2_wade.says: All SN2 reactions proceed with inversion of configuration.

wiki_halohydrin.says: Halohydrin formation from alkenes is anti addition leaving X and OH trans.

da_smith.cite: Smith, LibreTexts 14.13 Specific Rules Governing the Diels-Alder Reaction
da_smith.says: Diels-Alder reactions with cyclic dienes favour bicyclic products with substituents endo; cyclopentadiene is a locked s-cis diene that reacts rapidly.

ucla_chemosel.cite: UCLA Illustrated Glossary of Organic Chemistry, chemoselective
ucla_chemosel.says: NaBH4 reduces a ketone but leaves an ester unchanged (chemoselective); LiAlH4 reduces both ketone and ester.

wiki_carbred.says: Esters require stronger hydride reagents than aldehydes/ketones; hydrides generally do not attack C=C.

acetal_vs.cite: Vollhardt and Schore, LibreTexts 17.8 Acetals as Protecting Groups
acetal_vs.says: Acetals/ketals are unreactive in neutral to strongly basic media (inert to nucleophiles/organometallics) and are cleaved by aqueous acid; used to protect a ketone while an ester reacts.

conj_kenyon.cite: Kenyon College LibreTexts 18.10 1,2- and 1,4-Additions of Organometallic Reagents
conj_kenyon.says: Grignard reagents add irreversibly and kinetically, giving predominantly 1,2-addition to enones; Gilman (cuprate) reagents give 1,4-conjugate addition.

smith_unsat.says: Organocuprates (Gilman reagents) add to alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyls in a 1,4 (conjugate) fashion.

reusch_enolate.cite: Reusch, Virtual Textbook of Organic Chemistry: Reactions of Enolate-like Species
reusch_enolate.says: 2-Methylcyclohexanone under equilibrating (thermodynamic) enolate conditions with MeI gives mainly 2,2-dimethylcyclohexanone with poly-alkylation and ~20% SM; the kinetic (amide-base) route gives 2,6-dimethylcyclohexanone as chief product.

wiki_claisen.says: Heating allyl phenyl ether gives the 2-allylphenol (ortho) via [3,3] shift and tautomerisation; para product only when both ortho positions are blocked.

rad_uis.cite: LibreTexts 15.6 Chlorination versus Bromination (Morsch and Andrews, UIS CHE 269)
rad_uis.says: Light-induced bromination of propane at 25 C gives 97% 2-bromopropane (radical bromination is highly selective for the more substituted C-H); chlorination is much less selective.

cases.mechanism: acid-catalysed epoxide solvolysis, SN1-like at benzylic carbon

cases.title: 2-Bromobutane with NaOEt/EtOH: mixture of SN2 ether and E2 butenes, no single product

cases.title: 4-Nitroanisole bromination: Br ortho to OMe (and meta to NO2)
